questions.stem: On Wireframe and mockup: a designer reviewing a tech startup's pitch deck title slide notices that a team wants to test layout and flow before settling on colors. Which artifact suits this particular stage best?

options.text: A fully styled final mockup complete with all visual detail
options.misconception: commits to visual detail far too early in the process

options.text: A low-fidelity wireframe focused on structure and flow
A printed chart showing only the proposed color swatches
options.misconception: addresses only color, not layout or navigation

options.text: The final production code for the completed interface
options.misconception: is far too late a stage for early structural exploration

questions.explanation: A wireframe is a simplified, low-fidelity layout that focuses on structure and navigation without visual styling. It is ideal for testing flow early, while a mockup adds the visual design once the structure has been settled.
questions.hint: Which artifact strips away style in order to focus on structure?
